title: StarVoyager : Salvage and Shadows
author: jonhybee
selftext:
[](https://www.reddit.com/r/spacesimgames/?f=flair_name%3A%22Promotional%22)I am (also) working on a space game. I made this one for myself and my son. What we wanted was a an easy-to-setup and not too complex space ship simulator game where my 6yo can shoot laser in space using my full thrustmaster boeing yoke kit. I made the game based on Freelancer with a diablo style loot system. It can be played with any kind of inputs you would like and easy to customize (in theory).

Here is the trailer (turns out making these marketing videos is hard for me).

# [https://youtu.be/8wbPa1wpfMg](https://youtu.be/8wbPa1wpfMg)

The physics is "realism light" where the ship can be flown with flight assist where it will orient your vector into the ships nose automatically or you can point the ship and apply RCS/thrusters manually to accelerate or stop (but that is quite hard to manage).

I found that adding a "space brake" button helps a lot with the dog fighting.

I think the game might have an appeal for people that have a nice HOTAS setup and are looking for games where every button can be mapped to a ship's function. I play tested mostly with my thrustmaster boeing kit so the default mapping is probably nicer for this one.

I am a solo dev and have been working on this one for about 1 year now. I started with anti-gravity and free gemini and switched to a GPT plan with codex then switched to a codex-plug in for VS code. It looked much worse graphically until GPT Sol and Astra where the model making improved dramatically imo. 

I have been doing pass after pass after pass. I play test take notes then go back to my AI friend and chat about whats wrong/needs fixing. For me this game really does the job for what I was looking for and not finding which is a easy space game where you can have great input complexity (because of cockpit yoke, pedals and throttle setup).

I think the main story campaign and side missions are done, the gameplay loop is established and I really like the dogfight action so far. I am currently in the alpha playtest process trying to iron all the kinks out and make the tutorial a good experience for non-pilots (which is proving hard so far).

I have always dreamed of make games and though a lot about injecting the lore from r/conspiracy into a game, I wont spoil the main story but there is *stuff* in there \*wink\*.

Looking for feedback on the esthetique and concept, what do you NEED to have in such a game and do you absolutly do not want to see?

Do you think I will get hit with the S word? even if I do I dont really care, I have another job and game dev is  hobby for me. I am really curious about going through the whole steam game release process once so here we go!

Thank you!
